Hi everyone! We've been building MerLean-Prover, an agent for formalizing graduate-level mathematics in Lean, and wanted to share a few early results.

1. FormalQualBench. MerLean-Prover has completed the formalization of 10 problems on FormalQualBench — currently the most we're aware of for a single agent. We'd love to hear if others have pushed this further.

2. Stability. We took 4 problems spanning a range of difficulty and ran each 8 times. MerLean-Prover completed the formalization in every run, which gives us some confidence the harness is robust rather than getting lucky on individual attempts.

3. Not just frontier models. Beyond Opus, we ran the same harness with Sonnet and Haiku. On the 4-problem set, Sonnet completed all formalizations too — it just took several times longer than Opus. This suggests that graduate-level autoformalization with our harness is feasible even with lower-cost (and potentially open-source) models, not only the largest ones.

Full details are in our paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26959

Happy to answer questions and hear any feedback!

@Kevin Buzzard

Not yet. We are still improving the code to make it more user-friendly. In fact, we are rewriting everything using the OpenCode (it is currently built with the Claude Agent SDK, and Anthropic subscriptions will no longer be supported after June 15) so that it can easily support different models. We would like to release it once all of these improvements are complete.
